items.body:
**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Bind reset approval to the named redesign task**

When a reset record names redesign task A but reuses a `design_sha256` accepted in an unrelated task B, this query reports B's sender in `accepted_by`; the boundary check then treats the reset as anchored and suppresses both threshold and closed-unmerged warnings. The reset contract requires the acceptance RESULT to belong to the record's named `redesign_task`, but that field is never read or passed here, so the hash alone can bypass the reset backstop. Parse the named redesign task and require the matching RESULT's `task_id` to equal it.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.
items.disposition: fixed:324652e0

items.author: chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]
items.body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Report unanchored waivers outside the S2 branch**

When a task is below every S2 threshold but its PR is closed unmerged, a `DESIGN_RESET_WAIVED_BY=` line in either record is never reported because this check only runs inside the S2-reporting branch. The script still emits the closed-PR warning, but it hides the attempted unanchored waiver even though the documented trust control says every such line is surfaced as `waiver-unanchored`; perform this check independently of whether an S2 line exists or another anchor silences the threshold report.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.
items.disposition: fixed:324652e0

items.author: chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]
items.body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Correct the T119 amendment baseline**

The required acceptance replay says that 10 TASK messages should produce 8 amendments, but INV-6 and the implementation define amendments as TASKs minus one, and the exported fixture test correctly asserts 9. Following this completion criterion would therefore make a correct live result look wrong—or encourage an undercount to be accepted—so update the hand-computed baseline to 9 amendments.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.
items.disposition: not-applicable:the task.md on the branch is the byte-identical copy of the dispatched task file (69fee495, then d9a44b7e after amendment 1) and the worker may not change it; the finding is right on substance: INV-6's sentence gives 9 amendments for T119, the fixture test asserts 9, the acceptance replay compares against 9, and amendment 1 corrected the figure in the task file

items.author: chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]
items.body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Persist the commit ID required by the invariant**

This invariant says the Bot-head signal is backed by `original_commit_id` on `review_comment` items recorded by `pr-feedback.py`, but that collector currently drops both `original_commit_id` and `commit_id` when constructing review-comment items. The new counter can calculate the value only from the live API, so the acceptance evidence described here cannot reproduce or verify which heads were counted after GitHub state changes; persist the field in PR-feedback evidence or remove that unsupported evidence claim before the gate relies on it.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.
items.disposition: not-applicable:recording original_commit_id in scripts/pr-feedback.py is wave V3a's deliverable in the design map (V3a bullet) and pr-feedback.py is outside this task's allowed_files; A3 reads the field live with gh api and prints every counted head in its detail: line, which the acceptance record pins

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Restrict counted reviews to the Codex bot**

When another installed GitHub App posts comments using the same P0/P1 badge markup on two post-RESULT commits, checking only `.user.type == "Bot"` counts those heads and produces an INV-6 S2 boundary violation, even though INV-6 specifically limits this signal to the Codex Bot. The recorded fixtures identify that bot as `chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]`; filter on the expected login or stable app identity so unrelated automation cannot force a false redesign signal.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.
